1	# Waitlist site: what this kind of product is
2	
3	Read this first. This pack describes a one-page website that tests an idea by collecting sign-ups. It is not an online store. Where any instruction or example says "store" or "shopper", read "site" and "visitor".
4	
5	## What it is
6	
7	A single public page made of blocks in a default order (hero, product preview, benefits, waitlist form, footer), plus a small owner area where the owner reads the sign-ups and edits the words on the page.
8	
9	## Who it is for
10	
11	A founder with an idea who wants to know within days whether anyone cares, without spending a day on design, hosting and a sign-up database. Usually technical enough to judge the result, and short of time.
12	
13	## What good looks like
14	
15	- A visitor understands the promise in about five seconds and can join in under a minute, on a phone.
16	- The page looks credible: restrained, readable, well spaced, with one clear call to action.
17	- Every sign-up is stored once, with the answers to the form's questions and where the visitor came from.
18	- The owner sees at a glance how many people joined, progress toward their goal, which answers are most common, and can download the list.
19	- Nothing on the page is invented. Claims, numbers, testimonials and product screenshots come from the owner, or are left out, or are labelled as a concept.
20	
21	## What it is not
22	
23	No payments, no visitor accounts, no sending email in this version, no blog, no multi-page marketing site, no analytics suite. One page, one goal.
24	
25	## Principles
26	
27	- The page is blocks in an order, not a free canvas. The owner can hide a block and edit its words and images. Structure changes are change requests.
28	- The brief decides the words, the look and the form. These specs decide how everything behaves.
29	- When the brief is silent, choose a simple default and list it in AGENT_LOG.md under "Decisions on ambiguous points" so the owner can review it.

# AGENT_LOG: Tidewell waitlist site

## What I built and where

A one-page waitlist site for Tidewell (smart sleep ring) plus an owner area. Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript 5.9 strict, Drizzle + node-postgres, Tailwind 4 with CSS-variable roles, shadcn-style components (`src/components/ui`, Radix label/slot/alert-dialog), Zod at every boundary, Playwright in `e2e/`.

- **Database** (`src/db/schema.ts`, migration in `drizzle/`): `site` (one row), `blocks`, `form_fields`, `signups` (with `is_sample`), `images`, `rate_events` (in-database rate limit and sign-in lockout), `problems` (the "Recent problems" list).
- **Public page** (`src/app/page.tsx`, `src/components/site/*`): header with demo-notice bar, hero (split, photo on the right), integrations strip, preview (phone frame mock-up built in HTML/CSS, labelled "Concept preview"), benefits (rows layout, alternating), waitlist (heading + form card), footer. The page is server-rendered from the database on each request, so owner edits show on the next load.
- **Signup** (`src/app/api/signup/route.ts`, `src/lib/signup.ts`): honeypot, validation against the current fields and options, rate limit 5 per 10 minutes per first forwarded address, unique lower-cased email, cleaned source, problem recording.
- **Owner area** (`src/app/admin/...`): `/admin/sign-in`; `/admin` (total, today, goal progress, breakdown per select question, per source, list with search and pages of 50, delete with confirmation, delete all samples, CSV download, recent problems); `/admin/page` (panels Hero, Integrations, Preview, Benefits, Waitlist, Footer, each with show/hide and its own Save); `/admin/form` (questions, options, required, order, button label, thank-you message, privacy note); `/admin/settings` (name, tagline, description, contact email, accent, goal, goal start, demo notice).
- **Owner sign-in**: `ADMIN_EMAIL`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH` (`scrypt:<salt>:<hash>`), `SESSION_SECRET`, `DATABASE_URL`, listed in `.env.example`. Signed, httpOnly session cookie. Every `/admin` page checks the session in the layout, every server action and owner API checks it again (401 for APIs).
- **Scripts** in package.json: `db:migrate`, `db:seed` (does nothing if the site row exists), `hash-password` (prints only the hash), `db:generate`, `test:e2e`.
- **Images**: storage adapter in `src/lib/storage.ts` (local `.uploads/` served by `/uploads/[name]` in development, Vercel Blob when `VERCEL` is set; a deployed site without `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` shows a message on every upload field). JPEG/PNG/WebP up to 8 MB, type checked from the file's bytes, width and height stored, alt text required.
- **SEO**: title, description, Open Graph and Twitter tags from the settings, `lang="en"`, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, admin marked noindex (meta tag and `X-Robots-Tag` header) and disallowed.
- **Startup check**: `src/instrumentation.ts` validates the four settings and exits with a readable message naming the missing ones.

## Beyond the specs

- **Integrations block** (brief lists it between hero and preview): a quiet strip with the heading and two text-only chips (Apple Health, Google Health Connect). No logos. Own panel "Integrations" in `/admin/page`, own show/hide. Check: block order test and panel in owner area.
- **Demo notice bar** (brief `demo_notice: true`): a slim bar above the header, "Demonstration site. Nothing here is final." (my wording; the brief gives none). Editable on/off in Settings. The hero height subtracts the bar. Check: `demo notice is shown…`, `look: headline and main button visible…` at 375x667 and 1440x900.
- **Navigation from the brief** (How it works → preview, Why Tidewell → benefits, Contact → footer, button → waitlist): stored in `site.nav`, filtered at render time by visible blocks and by whether a contact email exists. Check: `W-014/15` tests.
- **Benefits `rows` layout** from the brief: one benefit per row, designed SVG panel on the alternating side, image above text on phones, lucide icon by the title. Check: the two `look:` row tests.
- **Hero background image + dimming setting** (edge W-018) on top of the split photo: owner can upload both; dimming none/soft/strong.
- **Removal line**: when a contact email exists the privacy note gets " To be removed from the list, email <address>." (edge W-030).
- **Benefit tools**: per-item hide, move up/down, add/remove (look.md says the owner can hide and reorder benefits).
- **Test hook**: `ENABLE_TEST_HOOKS=1` plus a header `x-test-fail: db` makes the signup route fail while saving, so W-009 is tested against the real handler. The variable is set only in `playwright.config.ts`.

## Decisions on ambiguous points

- **Look**: preset `dtc-brand`, as in the brief. Fonts: Fraunces 500/600 (headings) and DM Sans 400/500 (text), loaded with `next/font/google`. Colours exactly the preset's: background #FAF7F2, surface #FFFFFF, border #E7E0D6, text #1C1917, muted #6B635A. Radius 12px. Section padding 56px phone / 96px desktop. Hero headline 38/60px, section heading 28/38px, text 17/18px.
- **Accent**: the brief says to choose one muted accent and record it: **#3F6F73** (muted deep teal, "tide"). White on it is 5.6:1. Stored in `site.accent`; Settings refuses an accent where white text would drop under 4.5:1.
- **Brief wins over the preset**: the brief asks for a calm, light, airy page; the preset's light palette fits, so nothing was changed, except that the hero is a split layout (the brief) and that the hero gradient is built from accent and neutrals when there is no photo.
- **Hero dimming**: the brief says dimming "none" (it has no background image). If the owner adds a background image the text turns white and a dimming layer of at least 55% black is always applied (strong = 70%); "none" is raised to "soft" in that case so the 4.5:1 rule holds.
- **Placeholders**: hero photo is a designed ring illustration labelled "Ring photo"; preview is a phone frame with skeleton bars and the label "Concept preview". Neither contains invented words.
- **Benefits**: no per-benefit image upload; each row has a decorative SVG panel (aria-hidden, empty alt by nature).
- **Unconfirmed claims** (battery life, accurate sleep stages, privacy and not selling data): the brief lists three claims, all `confirmed: false`. None is shown anywhere. Sentences on the page that come from the brief and are not claims: hero subheadline, benefits, preview text, privacy note (copied verbatim). Note: the privacy note says "We'll only email you about Tidewell", though this version sends no email; it is the owner's approved text, so I kept it.
- **Rate limit** counts valid, non-honeypot submissions (including repeats of an email). Refused attempts are not counted again, so waiting ten minutes after the fifth frees the address.
- **Sign-in lockout**: locked when the last five failures fall within ten minutes and the newest is under ten minutes old. Failures from any email count against the address.
- **"Today"** in the owner area uses the server's day (UTC on Vercel). Dates in the list are shown in UTC.
- **Samples**: four labelled sample signups are seeded (`sample.*@example.com`). They are listed with a "Sample" label, left out of the total, today, goal, breakdowns, and included in the CSV with a Sample column.
- **Honeypot name**: `hp_4fz9kd` (random, written once in `src/lib/honeypot.ts`).
- **Source tracking**: the browser reads `?src=` (else `utm_source`) on load, keeps it in sessionStorage for the visit, and sends it; the server cleans it.
- **Form keys**: the brief's keys `full_name` and `email` are kept. The email field is stored only in the `email` column. New questions get a key made from their label.
- **Local database user**: the given `DATABASE_URL` has no user name and `pg` fails when `USER` is unset, so `src/db/connection.ts` adds the operating-system user when the URL has none. Real URLs with users are untouched.
- **Failed server in W-009**: if the database itself is down the problem is kept in memory and in the server log, and shown in the list once the page can load.
- **Process exit**: a missing setting makes the server print the message and exit with code 1 (a throw from the instrumentation hook left a server answering 500 to everything).
- **Sticky header** instead of the floating header of the deep-tech preset (dtc-brand does not specify one).
- **Copy-to-clipboard, trust block, before/after panel** from "moves from elite sites" were skipped: they need proof or commands the brief does not give.

## Not verified

- Visual quality was never looked at by eye (no way to view screenshots here); only measured with Playwright (viewport fit, overflow, alternation, contrast numbers).
- Real deployment (Vercel, Neon, Vercel Blob upload) was not tried. The Blob upload code path never ran; only the "no token" message was tested. Local-disk uploads were tested.
- Orphan-card check (look.md #4) does not apply: the page has no card grid (rows layout).
- Contrast was computed for text colours on their solid backgrounds, not over a real photo; over a photo I only checked that the overlay is dark enough for the worst case (white photo).
- Safari/Firefox, screen readers and real phones were not tried; only Chromium.
- W-012 only checks 3,000 rows complete, not memory use. W-031 is checked with a real process for a missing `ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH`, not for every variable (the function is unit-checked for the others).
- The `hash-password` script prints only the hash, but `npm run hash-password` itself prints npm's header lines; use `npm run --silent hash-password -- <password>` or `npx tsx scripts/hash-password.ts <password>`.

## Unclear, missing or misleading in the specs

- vision.md and experience.json talk about the "shopper" and "store" in the prompt, while the pack is a waitlist site; I read it as a waitlist site throughout.
- The edge file says the honeypot name must be `hp_` plus six random characters but `look.md` and the brief say nothing about where to keep it; I put it in one file shared by the form and the server.
- "Sample signups left out of every count" (W-027) vs "downloads all signups" (CSV): I include samples in the CSV with a Sample column.
- The brief's nav "Contact" targets the footer, while the requirements say Contact is a mailto link when there is a contact email. I kept the brief's anchor and put the mailto link in the footer.
- The spec says the dimming default is "soft unless the brief sets a value, which wins"; the brief says "none" yet requires 4.5:1. I resolved this as described above.
- "Seed data" for a waitlist: the spec wants labelled samples, but the deploy script runs `db:seed` on the live database too, so a live site starts with four labelled samples; the owner deletes them with one button.
- The brief's privacy note promises email although email is excluded from this version.

## Mistakes made and fixed

- The hero button still linked to `#waitlist` when the Waitlist block was hidden (a dead link). Found by the W-015 test; the button now disappears with the block.
- A throw in the instrumentation hook did not stop the server (it answered 500 forever and my test left stray servers running); now it exits, and the tests spawn Next directly and check the exit code.
- First sign-in tests matched two `alert` elements (Next's route announcer); scoped to the form.
- The no-reload check used `framenavigated`, which fires on Next's own history updates; replaced by a window marker that must survive the submit.
- A flaky image check (lazy image not loaded yet); now scrolls to it and polls.
- `pg` could not connect with the user-less `DATABASE_URL`; fixed by `connectionOptions()`.

## Final results

Commands run from the app folder (after the last code change):

- `npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0, no output.
- `npm run build` → "Compiled successfully", all routes listed (`/`, `/admin`, `/admin/form`, `/admin/page`, `/admin/settings`, `/admin/sign-in`, three API routes, `/uploads/[name]`, `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`), no warnings.
- `npm run db:migrate` → "Migrations applied."
- `npm run db:seed` (first run) → "Seeded the site, blocks, form fields and sample signups (labelled as samples)."; second run → "Site row already exists: nothing seeded."
- `npx playwright test --reporter=dot` (serves the production build on port 3100) → `50 passed (47.6s)`. Stderr lines were only the expected 404s for deliberately missing image files and the logged simulated failure from the W-009 test hook.

Owner sign-in for local testing: `ADMIN_EMAIL` in `.env`; the test password is `tidewell-dev-password` (its hash is in the local `.env`, which is not committed). Replace it before deploying.
